label: EdgeSwitch 16 PoE (150W)
description: EdgeSwitch 16 PoE (150W) (ES-16-150W) - 16x 1G RJ45 (16 PoE+) + 2x 1G SFP. All 16 copper ports are PoE/PoE+ (34.2 W per port class) against a 150 W budget; 24V passive PoE is available on the same ports.
notes: Census from the vendor tech-spec table (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/es-16-150w, HTTP 200, 574,980 B, read 2026-11-20): Networking interface "(16) 10/100/1000 Mbps RJ45 ports; (2) 1 Gbps SFP ports"; PoE interface "PoE/PoE+ (Pins 1, 2+; 3, 6-); 24V DC passive PoE (Pins 4, 5+; 7, 8-)"; max per port "PoE+: 34.2W; Passive PoE: 17W"; management "UART console Out-of-Band". The 16 copper ports were declared 1G/100M although the page states 10/100/1000 Mbps - the 10M rung is now modelled, matching the same fix PR #2249 made across the ECS family. Budget, now sourced: the live page prints "Power supply: AC/DC, internal, 150W" and "Max. power consumption: 150W" and no "Total PoE available" row, which is why the 150 W sat in the model name; Ubiquiti states the allocation in words on its own storefront instead - see `poe.note`. Census correction: the page's Management interface row reads "UART console Out-of-Band" and this spec declared only the 16 copper ports and 2 cages, so the console is added - 19 jacks, matching the page.

poe.note: Ubiquiti states the allocation, so 150 W is a published figure and not the model-name parse it used to be. The archived store page's key features list reads "(16) GbE PoE+ ports ... (2) SFP ports ... 150W total PoE availability ... Rack-mountable, 1U", and its spec table is the one the live tech-spec page still prints: "Power supply: AC/DC, internal, 150W", "Max. power consumption: 150W", "PoE interface: PoE/PoE+ (Pins 1, 2+; 3, 6-); 24V DC passive PoE (Pins 4, 5+; 7, 8-)", "Max. wattage per port: PoE+ 34.2W / Passive PoE 17W" - but with no "Total PoE available" row, which is the row the storefront supplies in prose. `dl.ui.com/ds/es-16-150w_ds.pdf` answers 302 to the techspecs root, so no datasheet exists to quote instead. Recorded caveat: 150 W of availability from a 150 W supply is tight, and Ubiquiti publishes no including/excluding split for this model (its UniFi sibling US-16-150W does: 150 W including / 28 W excluding = 122 W of availability). 150 W is modelled because the vendor states it as availability, not because it was derived here; a partial fill is capped by the per-port ceilings, not by this number.
